collection.description: A young traveller walks into the village carrying a map drawn on a stretched hide.

ask.text:
A young traveller walks into the village carrying a map drawn on a stretched hide. It's half finished. The island's coast is drawn in, wobbly but recognizable. The inland is entirely blank, except for one word in the middle: "?"
"I'm a mapmaker," the traveller says. "Well. An apprentice. Well. I'm trying." (He/She) asks (name) for work, any work at all, in exchange for being allowed to walk every trail on the island.
(Name) looks at the map. (His/Her) own hut, (he/she) notices, is drawn as a small blob labelled "goat?" (Name) isn't sure whether to be insulted or amused. Should (he/she) give this hopeful apprentice a chance?

choices.label: Ask If They Want to Stay On
Swap Trail Walks for Harvest Help

c1o1.text: The apprentice is given water, shade and a meal, and falls asleep almost at once, with the map clutched to (his/her) chest like a baby. (Name) gently corrects "goat?" to "hut" while (he/she) sleeps.

c1o2.text: The apprentice shares a pouch of smoked eel from (his/her) travels, which is chewy, strange and delicious. It adds a little food, and the children dare each other to eat it.

c1.text: (Name) decides that, before anything else, this sunburned person needs a drink...

c2o1.text: The apprentice shows how (he/she) measures distance by counting paces, and tying a knot in the cord every hundred steps, so (he/she) always knows how far (he/she) has walked. It's a simple, clever method, and it teaches the village something useful about maps. The builders start using it to lay out new huts.

c2o2.text: When (name) asks who taught (him/her) to make maps, the apprentice goes evasive. (He/She) won't say, and nobody insists. "Someone very good," is all (he/she) offers, "who didn't want to be found."

c2.text: (Name) asks how the apprentice is making the map. The apprentice brightens immediately and pulls out a long knotted cord...

c3o1.text: The apprentice decides to finish the map from here, using the village as a base, and joins the village permanently as a new adult villager. The finished map, some seasons later, is hung in pride of place. (Name)'s hut is correctly labelled. Mostly.

c3o2.text: The apprentice thanks them, but there is so much inland left to map, and (he/she) can't bear to stop. (He/She) walks on in the morning to map the next stretch, promising to bring back a copy.

c3.text: Seeing how happy the apprentice is walking the trails, (name) asks whether (he/she) might want to stay a while...

c4o1.text: Between trail walks, the apprentice helps with the harvest, and adds a good amount of food to the stores. (He/She) also maps every field in the village, which the farmers find extremely useful for arguing about who owns what.

c4o2.text: On the second day, rain warps the hide map badly, and the apprentice is in despair. The villagers help restretch it on a frame by the fire, slowly, until it's flat again, and send (him/her) onward with it, dry.

c4.text: (Name) agrees to the deal: help with the work in the mornings, walk the trails in the afternoons...
